summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for post-procedural pain management following a scheduled flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and excision of friable mucosa, due to recurrent tracheal stenosis from Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. The procedure was uncomplicated, and he was monitored on the internal medicine service. His pain was managed with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and short-term oxycodone, with successful weaning off opioids by discharge. His white blood cell count, initially elevated, normalized during the stay. Biopsy of the excised tissue showed squamous metaplasia and mild chronic inflammation without malignancy. Home prednisone was continued, and plans were made to restart pirfenidone as an outpatient. He remained stable, with improved respiratory symptoms and pain control, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up arranged.
